comments.content: This log line is emitted for the common, non-error case where the path simply doesn't end with a delimiter (which the code then fixes by appending one). Logging it as a "Warning" on every call will be noisy and misleading. Consider removing this log statement.
This `log.Printf("relativePath: %s", relativePath)` appears to be leftover debugging output that will fire for every path added to the tree. It should be removed before merging.

These log statements ("path already in tree", "invalid path component", "added to existing parent", "adding new path") look like debug logging that will be very verbose in production. Please remove them or gate them behind a debug flag.
Leftover debug log statement (`singleFile or includeDir; tarPathPrefix`). Consider removing before merge.
`log.Printf("writing %v", path)` fires per-entry during tar streaming and will be extremely noisy for large directories. Please remove this debug log.

Changing `GetParentPathString` to return `""` instead of `fspath.Separator` for the root case is a behavior change. `ReadTarStream` in s3fs uses the result as `tarPathPrefix`; please confirm callers handle an empty string correctly and that this doesn't produce malformed tar paths for top-level entries.

In `PrefixCopyRemote`, `CleanPathPrefix` is now called on `fspath.Join(destPathPrefix, next.Name)` but the returned `err` is only checked after the `if singleFile { fileName = destPath }` branch. When `singleFile` is true, `fileName` is overwritten with `destPath` but the earlier `err` from the Join-based CleanPathPrefix is still evaluated on the next line — while harmless, the control flow is confusing. More importantly, `CleanPathPrefix` now returns `nil` error for an empty path (changed below), so a genuinely empty computed path will silently pass. Please verify this cannot produce an empty destination key that overwrites the bucket root.

`CleanPathPrefix` now returns `("", nil)` for an empty path instead of an error. Previously an empty path was treated as invalid. This weakens a guard used across copy/delete paths — an empty prefix passed to S3 list/delete operations could match the entire bucket. Please confirm all call sites still reject empty paths where a non-empty prefix is required (e.g. destination keys).
